speaker: Arne Slot
quote_text:
John. Hello, Ali. But first off, we'll show out of  character to what your team has done this season.  
What to put down the performance in that first  laugh and generally today? I think especially 15  
minutes of the first half. I saw also parts before  we conceded or before we conceded the second one,  
normal parts for us. So I saw some very good  build-up situations, the way we positioned  
ourselves. So it wasn't 45 minutes of disaster.  But the errors we made, I think, is something  
we're not used to. And that's something different  than playing poorly. in my opinion. Yeah,  
sure. Well, I mean, it must have disappointed  you, don't it? Yes, of course. But not only me,  
the players themselves, the teammates, the fans,  it disappoints us all. But one of the reasons why  
we are in the position we are in is we don't make  a lot of mistakes. And if we do, players try to  
make up for them. Now, this is also what we tried  to do with the second goal. But unfortunately,  
instead of the ball being deflected, going in  behind, it went into goals. So this can happen,  
especially if you play a good team like Fulham. If  you make mistakes, they have the quality to punish  
us. And I think in the end, we created second-half  so many chances that we could have made-up for it.  
But we lacked time. We lacked time, especially in  the end, because in the first 20 minutes in the  
second-half, it didn't feel to me as if we could  score a goal. But in the last 20, 25 minutes,  
I think it was clear for everyone that we could  score the first. That's why actual playing time  
wasn't the most. in the last twenty-five minutes.  Given the advantage of what we had going into this  
game, do you think there was a bit of complacency  in the past half or do you think it was just  
errors? Nah, I think it's the last thing. I think  there's no reason for us to be complacent because  
we are not leading. We're not number one at the  moment because we win every game with a margin of  
three or four goals. I think everyone that has  seen our games, it takes us so much effort, so  
much hard work to win games of football combined  with quality, of course. But yeah, the team that  
won the league the last four seasons were already  freeing up at halftime every single game almost  
they played. And that's not the way it is for us.  So we are fully aware of the fact that we have to  
compete for seven now, it is, I think, seven  more games. We showed, we showed on Wednesday  
when Everton was close call. Today was a close  call, and many times we've been on the right side,  
today we're on the wrong side, mainly because of  the errors we made. There's a couple of moments  
of uncertainty with Virgil van Dijk, probably has  been in the last couple of games. Does that come  
with the territory of being this late in the  season, or is it something you could probably  
look in deeper and criticise? I mainly give credit  to other players as well. So if you look at Beto,  
he's not the first defender who finds it difficult  to play against Beto because he's so every time  
he's chasing for every ball, pushes it just before  you get the ball. And yeah, the one that played  
there today was also, you have to give credits  to him as well. I think I still see a lot, a lot,  
a lot of things that Virgil does really well. And  if you play 50, 60 games of seasons, there will  
be also, even for him, one or two moments where he  could have done better. But in general, I think if  
I look at Virgil's performance against Everton,  except for this one time he missed the ball, he  
was outstanding. So I don't worry about him. What  was your message to the players afterwards? And  
would you agree that the league table still looks  unbelievable for you? with seven games to go. The  
message was mainly that I think I told them that  they showed great character the second-half,  
but not for the first time this season. We had  a difficult first half. It didn't happen a lot,  
but I can come up with Southampton at home,  for example, where we played quite poorly.  
And normally we are able to make up for  that because of the mentality of the team,  
how fit they are, the steps we can bring.  But today it wasn't enough and now we have  
a whole week to prepare for West Ham and everyone  needs to be aware and they are. So I didn't have,  
actually I didn't even have to tell them, but  the only way we can win a game of football  
is by hard work, 90 minutes, constant effort,  because I've said it I think a few times now,  
we are not the team that's leading at  halftime with three or four nil with three,  
4, 5 acts of brilliance. It's hard work every time  we've won a league a game of football this season,  
except for two or three games. You only made the  one change, obviously, for the derby in midweek.  
Considering how flat it was for section of that  first half, do you regret not freshening it up to  
a greater extent? No, no, no. Not because of  that reason, because I think there were four  
days in between. And we've showed many times this  season that that's not a problem at all for us,  
these players as well. And I don't think the  errors we've made had anything to do with players  
being tired. And again, I know how it works. It's  everywhere the same in football. If you concede  
three goals in the first half, everybody's like,  wow, that was a disaster. Now, if you look back  
at it, knowing that you concede three, you will  probably see a few good moments as well. because  
there were also good moments from us in build-up.  I think after half an hour I looked at the,  
it was one-all. I was like, okay, it's not our  best game, but we have control over the game.  
But then all of a sudden I blinked my eyes and  we were free one down. Thank you. Thank you.
title: Arne Slot post-match press conference | Fulham 3-2 Liverpool
